content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged brown bear frame. Host frame: the brown bear sets the outline, body size and overall frame. A single creature that combines a european rhinoceros beetle and a brown bear. Head of the brown bear, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: brown bear body and legs, with its own dense fur everywhere else, plain coat, no stripes or spots; from the european rhinoceros beetle, as parts and materials on the brown bear's own body: a single curved horn of hard, glossy chitin rising from the brow; hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors, in a few large patches over the back and flanks, with clean edges, color and surface unchanged inside each patch. Coat texture and patches follow the body outline. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs and visible breathing openings along the flanks. Bilaterally symmetrical, recognizable limbs, visible sense organs. Habitat cue (forest): dark back and light belly (mild countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.

summary.text:
**Planning beetle illustration**
I'm deciding to look up European rhinoceros beetle references to guide the arthropod anatomy, countershading, and natural-history pose for a full-body, side three-quarter illustration.
**Designing hybrid creature image**
I'm planning a single creature with a four-legged brown bear silhouette and head, adding a curved glossy chitin horn on the brow and a few large, clean-edged beetle plates over the back and flanks while keeping dense, plain fur elsewhere.
**Creating detailed beetle image**
I'm generating the detailed beetle illustration now, using the references to guide the subject, texture, and composition for a clear, high-detail final image.
**Refining beetle chitin coverage**
I'm adjusting the design to use fewer, larger chitin patches across the back and flanks, and reducing the amount on the legs for a cleaner look.
